title: Volkswagen Golf 2017
summary: Five-door hatchback. All four doors, the bonnet and the tailgate open, and every panel comes off.
real_layout: Transverse engine at the front driving the front wheels (four-wheel drive on some versions): the same layout as the teaching engine.

title: Nissan Qashqai 2018
summary: Compact SUV, for years the UK's best seller. All four doors, the bonnet and the tailgate open.
real_layout: Transverse engine at the front driving the front wheels (four-wheel drive on some versions): the same layout as the teaching engine.

title: BMW 3 Series Touring 2014
summary: Five-door estate (the F31 Touring) with a tall tailgate.
real_layout: The real car's engine sits lengthways at the front and drives the rear wheels (xDrive versions drive all four). The teaching engine shown is transverse front-drive, so the real layout differs.

title: Land Rover Defender Works V8 Trophy 2021
summary: The classic Defender 110 body, built new by Land Rover Classic in 2021: five doors and a side-hinged rear door.
real_layout: The real Works V8 has a 5.0-litre V8 mounted lengthways at the front and permanent four-wheel drive. The teaching engine shown is transverse front-drive, so the real layout differs.

title: Porsche 911
summary: Rear-engined sports coupe: the luggage space is at the front, the engine at the back.
real_layout: A flat-six engine behind the rear axle drives the rear wheels (Carrera 4 and Turbo versions drive all four). The teaching engine is placed at the back to show where the engine lives; the real one is a flat-six, not an inline four.

title: Renault Master
summary: Large panel van: hinged cab doors, a sliding door on each side and barn doors at the back, each hinged at its outer edge.
real_layout: Engine at the front; most versions drive the front wheels, heavier ones the rear.

title: Nissan NV200 2010
summary: Small panel van: a sliding door on each side and two barn doors at the back.
real_layout: Transverse engine at the front driving the front wheels: the same layout as the teaching engine.

title: Mercedes-Benz Vito
summary: Mid-size panel van: a sliding door on the right and two barn doors at the back. The model has no left sliding door.
real_layout: The real van's engine sits lengthways at the front and drives the rear wheels (some versions drive all four). The teaching engine shown is transverse front-drive, so the real layout differs.

title: Mercedes-Benz Sprinter 2019
summary: Large van: hinged cab doors, a sliding door on each side and two barn doors at the back.
real_layout: The real van's engine sits lengthways at the front and drives the rear wheels (some versions drive all four; a front-drive version mounts it across the front). The teaching engine shown is transverse front-drive, so the usual layout differs.

title: Volkswagen ID. Buzz
summary: Electric people carrier: hinged front doors, a sliding door on each side and a tailgate.
real_layout: Electric: a motor at the back drives the rear wheels (the GTX adds one at the front), with the battery under the floor. It has no engine.

title: Heavy cruiser motorbike
summary: A 45-degree V-twin cruiser modelled in code to a Fat Boy-style bike's published sizes. Forty parts come off.
real_layout: Engine in the middle of the frame, gearbox behind it, primary drive on the left and a belt to the rear wheel.

steps.text: Tyres and wheels: pressures cold, tread depth across the width, no cuts, bulges or nails; wheels true with no cracks.
Controls: levers and pedals move freely and return; the throttle snaps shut on its own with the bars at full lock both ways.
Lights and electrics: headlamp high and low, tail and brake lamp from both brakes, all four indicators, horn.
Oil and fluids: engine oil level on the level ground, no leaks from the crankcase, primary or gearbox; brake fluid between the marks.
Chassis: fork seals dry and the fork smooth when you push the front down; rear shocks not leaking; belt tension and teeth.
Stand: the side stand springs fully up on its own and holds the bike when down.
Front: pads thicker than the wear line, the disc smooth with no deep scoring or blueing.
Rear: the same check at the rear caliper and disc; the pedal firm, not spongy.
The two cylinders sit in a 45-degree V on one crankcase; each has a finned barrel for air cooling and a head on top.
Pushrods in the chromed tubes carry the cam's lift up to the rockers under the rocker covers, which open the valves.
Air comes in through the air cleaner on the right; burnt gas leaves through the two exhaust pipes.

title: Supersport motorbike
summary: A 600 cc inline-four supersport modelled in code to an R6-style bike's published sizes. Fifty-nine parts come off, from the fairing panels to the chain.
real_layout: Inline four across the frame, leaning forward, with the gearbox in the same cases behind the crank; a chain drives the rear wheel.

steps.text: Tyres and wheels: pressures cold, tread depth across the width, no cuts, bulges or nails; wheels true with no cracks.
Controls: levers and pedals move freely and return; the throttle snaps shut on its own with the bars at full lock both ways.
Lights and electrics: both headlamps high and low, tail and brake lamp from both brakes, all four indicators, horn.
Oil and coolant: engine oil level on level ground with the bike upright, no leaks from the cases; coolant between the marks, hoses firm.
Chassis: fork seals dry, the shock not leaking; chain slack within the figure, the chain lubed, sprocket teeth not hooked.
Stand: the side stand springs fully up on its own and holds the bike when down.
Front: two discs, a radial caliper on each fork leg; pads thicker than the wear line, the discs smooth with no deep scoring or blueing.
Rear: the same check at the rear caliper and disc; the pedal firm, not spongy.
Take off the side panels: the radiator sits behind the front wheel, the exhaust headers run down in front of the engine.
Four cylinders in one block lean forward; the head and the cam cover sit on top, a coil on each spark plug.
Air comes in through the airbox under the tank and four throttle bodies into the back of the head.
The clutch sits behind its cover on the right, the alternator behind its cover on the left; the oil filter is at the front, low down.
Under the seat and its side covers: the battery and the subframe.

title: 125 cc scooter
summary: A 125 cc scooter modelled in code to a PCX125-style scooter's published sizes. The seat lifts over the storage bin, both stands swing down and fifty parts come off.
real_layout: A single cylinder lying forward under the seat, driving the rear wheel through a belt CVT; engine and drive swing with the rear wheel.

steps.text: Tyres and wheels: pressures cold, tread depth across the width, no cuts, bulges or nails; wheels true with no cracks.
Controls: both brake levers firm and returning; the throttle snaps shut on its own with the bars at full lock both ways.
Lights and electrics: headlamp high and low, tail and brake lamp from both levers, all four indicators, horn.
Oil and coolant: engine oil on the dipstick with the scooter on its centre stand, coolant between the marks.
Chassis: fork seals dry, both rear shocks not leaking; the stands spring up on their own.
Front: pads thicker than the wear line, the disc smooth with no deep scoring.
Rear: a drum brake in the hub; the lever's free play within the figure, the wear indicator inside its range.

procedures.title: Under the seat and the panels

steps.text: Lift the seat: the storage bin is under it; the battery sits behind it, under the tail.
The fuel tank lies under the floorboard, between the frame's tubes.
The engine and its CVT case form one unit that swings with the rear wheel: the cylinder lies forward, the belt drive runs back in the case on the left.
Air comes in through the filter box on top of the case; the exhaust runs under the engine to the silencer on the right.
